{{short description|American chemical engineer}}

'''Julie Spicer England''' (born November 12, 1957) is an American chemical engineer and business executive, who served as Vice President of [[Texas Instruments Incorporated]].<ref>{{cite web |title=WITI Hall of Fame - Julie Spicer England |url=http://www.witi.com/center/witimuseum/halloffame/121795/Julie-Spicer-England-Vice-President,-Texas-Instruments-Incorporated-General-Manager-RFid-Systems/ |publisher=Women in Technology International |date=1998 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131007063716/http://www.witi.com/center/witimuseum/halloffame/121795/Julie-Spicer-England-Vice-President,-Texas-Instruments-Incorporated-General-Manager-RFid-Systems/ |archive-date=7 October 2013}}</ref>

Born in [[Wisconsin Rapids, Wisconsin]], England obtained her BA in Chemical Engineering in 1979 and later her MBA, both from the [[Texas Tech University]].<ref>''Who's who in the South and Southwest,'' 2005. p. 192</ref> After her graduation she started her lifelong career at Texas Instruments Incorporated. In 1998 she was inducted into the Women in Technology International Hall of Fame (WITI),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://witi.com/halloffame/121795/Julie-Spicer-England-Independent-Board-Advisor-TTM-Technologies/|title=WITI - Julie Spicer England|website=witi.com|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref> and in 2004 was awarded the [[Henry Laurence Gantt Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.asme.org/about-asme/honors-awards/achievement-awards/henry-laurence-gantt-medal|title=Henry Laurence Gantt Medal|website=www.asme.org|language=en|access-date=2020-01-22}}</ref>
